off.label: AI off
off.text: Student AI is off. Use the demonstration, documentation, and human help.

questions.label: AI: questions
questions.text: AI may answer questions and explain. It may not write, complete, or rewrite your code.

completion.label: AI: completion
completion.text: AI may complete a line or block you started. You explain every completion you keep.

scoped.label: AI: scoped
scoped.text: AI may write code inside a scope you set and describe. You test it and explain it.

week-0.focus: Enter the course by locating your work and tracing one visible change to its source.

principle.plain: Compare the page before and after one source edit before naming what changed.

outcomes.text: State what Canvas, the course site, and your repository each hold.
Predict what a Markdown mark will change. Make the change without AI. Compare the preview with your prediction.
Accept the Workspace assignment. Commit a first edit in your own private repository.
Answer the four introduction questions in Markdown in your repository. Submit the repository link.

week-0.draft: Week 0 Canvas work is linked from the lessons. The detailed outcome mapping and Attend placement in Apply still await instructor review.

week-1.focus: Give Project 1 meaningful structure before styling it.

principle.plain: Choose ordered steps and unordered ingredients because they carry different kinds of content.

outcomes.text: Structure Project 1 with meaningful headings, unordered ingredients, and ordered steps.
Explain the Project 1 list choice after moving one step outside its list in a copy.
Credit one permitted Project 1 image with purposeful alternative text and a descriptive source link.
Test the Project 1 source link, image, and latest saved HTML before delivery.

week-1.draft: Waits on Travis to settle the visual-note evidence and approve the Kinds placement in Apply.

week-2.focus: Make Project 1 readable with CSS and connect each visible result to its source.

principle.plain: Compare each spacing prediction with the browser result, even when the prediction felt certain.

outcomes.text: Explain how a selector and declaration create the Project 1 type hierarchy and spacing.
Predict a margin or padding change, make it without AI, and compare the visible result.
Publish a readable Project 1 whose headings, lists, image credit, and source link survive narrow widths.
Repair a supplied nesting or class-name fault without AI and verify the saved result.

week-2.draft: Waits on Travis to approve the Confidence placement in the Project 1 lesson.

week-3.focus: Move Project 1 into one published repository and plan Project 2 with real content.

principle.plain: Separate saving, committing, pushing, and publishing while tracing one change to the live page.

outcomes.text: Trace a relative path from the Project 2 file to the Project 1 folder and test the destination.
Commit, push, and verify one manual Project 1 change on its published page.
Plan the real Project 2 content and reading order in one wide Figma frame.
Credit two Project 2 sources beside the planned content and one permitted image.
Ask AI to explain one Project 2 path or commit message, then check its answer against documentation.

week-3.draft: Waits on Travis to approve Week 3 as the start of the questions stage.

week-4.focus: Turn the Project 2 plan into a flexible composition and repair one observed layout problem.

principle.plain: Make a layout prediction, test it at 375px, and keep room for the browser to prove it wrong.

outcomes.text: Arrange the Project 2 figure and introduction with Flexbox while preserving meaningful source order.
Predict how removing flex-wrap affects Project 2 at 375px, then restore the safer behavior.
Repair one observed Project 2 layout problem and verify it at narrow and wide widths.
Publish Project 2 with readable content, working sources, keyboard focus, and a route home.

week-4.draft: Waits on Travis to approve the Mistaken placement in the Project 2 lesson.

week-5.focus: Build a repeatable Project 3 pattern and test its columns through supported independent practice.

principle.plain: Use results at 375px and 1000px to support the column explanation instead of relying on appearance alone.

outcomes.text: Build three Project 3 entries from one reusable semantic card pattern.
Predict and test gap and column changes at 375px and 1000px.
Explain which media-query rule applies at each tested width from browser evidence.
Name an exact blocker after two focused repair attempts on the practice starter.

week-5.draft: Waits on Travis to keep Week 5 in the questions stage before completion begins.

week-6.focus: Adapt Project 3 when its content becomes crowded and test its navigation across widths.

principle.plain: Watch where Project 3's content becomes crowded before choosing a breakpoint.

outcomes.text: Choose a Project 3 breakpoint where its cards or navigation begin to crowd.
Build a semantic Project 3 section and repair one selector or path fault without AI.
Test the Project 3 anchors, focus, images, and text at narrow, intermediate, and wide widths.
Explain the active responsive rule immediately below and above the chosen breakpoint.
Accept one AI completion in Project 3, test it in the browser, and explain the line you kept.

week-6.draft: Waits on Travis to approve Week 6 as the start of the completion stage.

week-7.focus: Use browser evidence to repair and publish Project 3 as a usable responsive page.

principle.plain: Show the original symptom, exact cause, repair, and passing test before calling Project 3 fixed.

outcomes.text: Locate one Project 3 fault using browser or source evidence before changing code.
Repair the fault, reproduce its original test, and check one neighboring condition.
Publish Project 3 as a responsive page with three accurate entries, reliable navigation, credits, and keyboard focus.
Verify Project 3's public page signed out at narrow, intermediate, and wide widths.
Set a written scope for AI code in Project 3, test the result, and revise one part yourself.

week-7.draft: Waits on Travis to approve Week 7 as the start of scoped code writing.

week-8.focus: Design one truthful Project 4 invitation and translate two frames into one document.

principle.plain: Revise one confusing hierarchy or action after a peer tries to identify the offering and next step.

outcomes.text: State the Project 4 audience, offering, and primary action in three concise sentences.
Plan the real Project 4 content at 375px and 1280px in Figma.
Build one semantic Project 4 structure with a flexible hero or feature group.
Explain how the same HTML changes arrangement between widths after one peer revision.

week-8.draft: Waits on Travis to approve the Revisable placement in the Project 4 Apply lesson.

week-9.focus: Make Project 4's primary action truthful and keyboard usable.

principle.plain: Compare the action's promised result with what actually happens when you activate it.

outcomes.text: Choose a link, button, or labeled form that matches the actual Project 4 behavior.
Reach and activate the primary Project 4 action by keyboard with visible focus.
State the expected and observed action result, including whether it sends any data.
Repair one misleading interaction or confirm its destination at a narrow width.

week-9.draft: Waits on Travis to approve the Confidence placement in the interaction Apply lesson.

week-10.focus: Finish Project 4, repair delivery faults, and curate the existing portfolio.

principle.plain: Prioritize broken behavior and unreadable content, then revise the portfolio without starting a new direction.

outcomes.text: Repair the highest-impact Project 4 failure and verify the published result signed out.
Publish Project 4 with a truthful primary action, working links, readable layouts, and visible focus.
Curate four project entries with introductions, working return paths, credits, and a repository link.
Explain and modify one source decision independently during the portfolio presentation.
Commit the final portfolio version and test every project link while signed out.

week-10.draft: Waits on Travis to approve the Revisable placement across Project 4 delivery and portfolio curation.
